source.title: Differentiation and Specialization of Attention Heads via the Refined Local Learning Coefficient
source.authors: George Wang; Jesse Hoogland; Stan van Wingerden; Zach Furman; Daniel Murfet

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes induction-head behavior and its timing in two-layer attention-only transformers. It reports staggered development of the two induction heads, refining a picture in which induction heads develop together at one transition.
record.gate_note: The paper also cites the original induction-head account and related results, which are not rows. Its main contribution is rLLC-based head analysis; the key timing results combine rLLC curves with an in-context-learning score. The loss-curve bump described in V2 is not directly tested.
record.test_reason: The study's own results bear on several versions in two-layer attention-only transformers. Token-in-context ablation analysis identifies induction behaviour in 1:6 and 1:7 (V1). Per-head ICL scores and GitHub drLLC curves show the two induction heads forming several thousand steps apart, each coinciding with its own ICL-score drop (V2, V7). Three extra seeds each develop at least one induction head (V4). The staggered-formation result is a specific refinement of the single-transition picture.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that refined LLCs reveal how attention heads differentiate into functional types and specialize to data, e.g. induction head 1:6 partly specialized to code. They also report that the refined LLCs uncover a new multigram circuit. As a secondary 'bonus' result, the two induction heads form at different times, each matching its per-head ICL-score drop, and the joint-head critical point coincides with the end of the ICL-score drop.
record.recipe_differences: The work studies the same broad two-layer attention-only induction-head setting, but uses refined LLC trajectories and token-in-context classifications, with mean ablations and an ICL score to investigate timing rather than reproducing the original circuit analysis directly.
record.method_sensitivity: Induction-head critical points differ by head; the paper also reports that developmental curves and some stage boundaries vary with evaluation data distribution and LLC-estimation hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Data-refined LLC on GitHub code pulls apart the two induction heads, whose wrLLCs are nearly identical at the end of training: 1:6 is much higher. Ablation examples show 1:6 handles induction patterns with punctuation and symbols, while 1:7 handles natural language.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distinct induction heads within one model specialize to different data subdistributions (e.g., code vs natural language).

record.problems: The main timing evidence relies on rLLC critical points as indicators of formation rather than a direct onset measure. The text gives no numerical ICL-score values or uncertainty estimates for the timing results, and does not test the claimed training-loss bump. The LLC estimator's accuracy is not guaranteed by the authors; they note that its justification presumes a local minimum, which may not hold during training.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were omitted. Other rLLC, Hessian, clustering, and multigram-circuit results do not measure the claim versions beyond the results recorded above.

untested.parts: Causal composition of induction heads with layer-0 previous-token heads. This is only indirectly visible in the K-composition plots, which no row records.
The training-loss bump and abruptness in the original sense. Figure 13 says the stages may be hidden from the training loss.
Entire version; no large models are studied.
Other model families, sizes, architectures and modalities; only same-setup seeds are tested.
Entire version. Data is varied only for evaluation and refinement, never for training.
Sub-steps within a single head's formation. Only the between-head staggering is shown.

missing.what: K-composition scores between previous-token heads (0:1, 0:4) and induction heads over training. The Hessian section says previous-token heads' plateau lasts until their composition with induction heads peaks. This bears on the composition part of V1.
Statement that stagewise development, including the induction stage, may be hidden from the training loss. This bears on the loss-bump part of V2.
Ablation scores showing that 1:7 is clearly distinguished by an increase in LM4, while 1:6 is less distinct. This is a behavioural timing measure for the two heads.

record.verdict_notes: Hoogland et al. (2024) used the same model and run; it is not an original source here, but R8 duplicates its run. The timing evidence combines a complexity proxy (drLLC) with a behavioural ICL score; only the ICL-score rows (R5–R7) bear on V2. No numeric ICL values or uncertainties are given. The record's V2 'challenges' label was replaced: the staggering qualifies the single-window picture but does not show the effect absent. The V4 limits_scope label on head count was removed, because count is not part of V4.

versions.untested_parts: The paper identifies induction-pattern behavior, but does not directly establish the causal composition of an earlier previous-token head with an induction head.
It does not measure a training-loss bump or establish that head formation is abrupt in the stated sense; timing is inferred from rLLC critical points and ICL-score curves.
The study does not test whether induction heads explain most ICL in large transformers.
The additional runs use the same two-layer attention-only model setup; other model families, sizes, architectures, and modalities are not tested.

The paper changes the evaluation/data-refinement distribution, including to GitHub code, but does not vary the training data or setup to test their effects on induction-head formation or persistent ICL.
Few-shot task learning through mechanisms other than repeated-token copying is not tested.
The paper reports staggered timings for the two induction heads, but does not comprehensively decompose formation into all possible sub-steps.

statements.correction: R1: head 1:6; 50k-step checkpoint; top 1k loss-affected tokens in context selected from 100k training samples using mean ablation; induction-pattern classification. Remove this study's row citation from the random-token experiment.
statements.problem: The statement describes another source's experiment but attaches this study's R1. R1 does not report random-token sequences, shuffled controls, or the listed sample counts.

statements.correction: Appendix C.1: most full-weight drLLCs respect the original stage boundaries; some LM3 decreases flatten or shift from 6.5k–8.5k to 5.5k–8k steps; authors attribute the shifts more likely to changing nβ from 23 to 30 than to the datasets.
statements.problem: The statement presents evaluation distribution and estimation hyperparameters as separately established causes of boundary variation; the paper explicitly identifies their confounding.
This study's formation–ICL correspondence is supported. Cross-study counts and other studies' findings are outside this check.

statements.correction: Appendices F.1 and G: four runs of an approximately 3M-parameter two-layer attention-only transformer trained on a DSIR-filtered Pile subset; original run reused from Hoogland et al. (2024); three additional seeds; induction-head counts 2, 1, 1, 2.
statements.problem: The seed counts and head identities are correct, but the conditions incorrectly exclude this study from natural-text run-variation evidence.
No study-specific factual assertion is identified here; the aggregate counts and other studies cannot be checked against this paper.

statements.correction: Appendix B.2.2 and Figure 10: head 1:7 develops several thousand steps before 1:6; separate timing is supported by drLLC critical points and per-head ICL scores; transition overlap is not quantified.
statements.problem: Within-head overlap is untested, but the paper also does not report measured temporal overlap between the two heads' transitions.

statements.correction: Appendix C.1: developmental trajectories differ across evaluation datasets; most stage boundaries persist; authors consider the slight boundary shifts more likely due to altered LLC-estimation hyperparameters than dataset differences.
statements.problem: The LLC-proxy description is correct, but distributional variation and hyperparameter effects are not independently established.
